title: Counting to birth: 38 or 40 weeks?

objective.text: Explain how doctors and embryologists each count the length of a pregnancy.

body.general: Is a pregnancy 40 weeks long, or 38? Doctors count 280 days, or 40 weeks, from the first day of the last period [f2]. Counted from fertilization, when egg and sperm join, birth comes about 266 days, or 38 weeks, later [f1]. The period date is used because the day of fertilization is rarely known [f4]. Sperm can wait several days for the egg [f4]. The period rule works best when cycles are regular [f5]. Most babies arrive within two weeks of the due date [f7].
body.mbbs: Birth occurs about 266 days (38 weeks) after fertilization [f1]. Obstetricians date pregnancy as 280 days (40 weeks) from the first day of the last normal menstrual period (LNMP) [f2]. The two clocks differ by about 2 weeks [f1,f2]. Fertilization usually follows ovulation within about 12 hours [f3]. Sperm survive up to about 6 days, so the exact date of fertilization is rarely known [f4]. LNMP dating assumes a regular 28-day cycle [f5]. Irregular cycles, or implantation bleeding about 14 days after fertilization, can mislead it [f6]. Most babies arrive within 10–14 days of the due date [f7]. Much earlier is premature; much later is postmature [f8]. Fetal age is also judged from length, weight and external form [f9]. Ultrasound crown–rump length (CRL) is the measure of choice in weeks 7–14 [f9]. The book gives its accuracy as 1–2 days [f12]. From weeks 16–30, biparietal diameter, head and abdominal circumference and femur length are used [f10].

facts.text: Birth comes about 266 days (38 weeks) after fertilization.
Obstetricians count pregnancy as 280 days (40 weeks) from the first day of the last normal menstrual period.
Fertilization usually happens within about half a day of ovulation.
Sperm can survive up to about 6 days, so the day of fertilization is rarely known exactly.
facts.note: R05aq: conception only from a 6-day window ending on ovulation day

facts.text: Dating from the last period works best when cycles are regular, about 28 days long.
Irregular cycles, or bleeding at implantation about 14 days after fertilization mistaken for a period, can make the date wrong.
Most babies are born within 10 to 14 days of the due date.
Babies born much earlier than this are premature; much later, postmature.
Fetal age can also be judged from length, weight and form; ultrasound crown–rump length (CRL) is the tool in weeks 7 to 14.
From about weeks 16 to 30, ultrasound uses head width (biparietal diameter), head and abdominal circumference and femur length.
Before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy, counted from the last period, a birth is preterm; the book puts this at about 12 % of US births.
The book gives ultrasound CRL in weeks 7 to 14 as accurate to within 1–2 days.
facts.note: D-044 (b), default until the owner decides: book answer in main

facts.text: ⚑ Newer evidence (D-044): one CRL scan dates a pregnancy to within about ±5 days (95 %); three scans, to about ±3 days.
facts.note: D-044 (b). R05ar: ±4.7 d one scan, ±2.7 d three (95 %); R05as: −7 to +4 d vs known insemination; the book's 1–2 d may mean measuring precision, not dating error

facts.text: Beyond Langman: even when timed exactly from ovulation, natural pregnancies vary in length by about 5 weeks.
facts.note: R05ap: range ~37 d even without preterm births

misconceptions.right: The 40 weeks count from the last period; from fertilization it is about 38 weeks (266 days).

checks.prompt: About how long after fertilization is a baby usually born?
checks.why: 280 days (40 weeks) is counted from the last period; fertilization comes about 2 weeks later, so birth is about 266 days after it.

checks.prompt: Why do obstetricians date pregnancy from the last menstrual period?
options: The day of fertilization is rarely known, but the period start usually is
Fertilization happens on the first day of the period
The embryo starts growing at the period
Fertilization always happens on the day of sex
checks.why: Sperm can survive for days and fertilization follows ovulation, not sex, so its date is rarely known.

checks.prompt: A due date is set 280 days after the last period began. When is birth most likely?
options: Within about 10–14 days of the due date
About a month before the due date
About three weeks after the due date
checks.why: The due date is an estimate; most babies arrive within 10–14 days of it.

clinical: A birth before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy, counted from the last period, is called preterm [f11]. The book puts this at about 12 % of births in the US [f11]. Knowing the due date well is what lets a birth be judged early or late [f7,f8].

remember.q: How long after fertilization is birth?
How do obstetricians count pregnancy length?
remember.a: 280 days, or 40 weeks, from the first day of the last period [f2].

remember.q: Why is pregnancy dated from the last period?
remember.a: Because the day of fertilization is rarely known exactly [f4].
